title: Derived tensor and K-flat representative descent on a ringed site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the universe of module sheaves and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Let $K(R)$ be the homotopy category of complexes of $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $Q_R:K(R)\to D(R)$ the localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal P_R$ be the full subcategory of $K(R)$ of K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and let $W_R$ be its quasi-isomorphisms. The induced functor $W_R^{-1}\mathcal P_R\to D(R)$ is an equivalence. The total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] induces a bifunctor $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-:D(R)\times D(R)\to D(R)$ with canonical isomorphisms $Q_R\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RQ)\cong Q_RP\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q_RQ$ for $P,Q\in\mathcal P_R$, natural in both homotopy-category variables and compatible with inversion of quasi-isomorphisms. For any category $E$ and bifunctors $U,V:D(R)\times D(R)\to E$, a natural transformation $U\to V$ is uniquely determined by its restriction along $Q_R|_{\mathcal P_R}\times Q_R|_{\mathcal P_R}$, and any natural transformation on that restriction extends uniquely.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$, which is abelian by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. By [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], every object of $K(R)$ receives a quasi-isomorphism from an object of $\mathcal P_R$. Quasi-isomorphisms in $K(R)$ have right calculus of fractions by [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system]. This calculus restricts to $W_R$: identities and composites are unchanged; given a right Ore square in $K(R)$ for arrows between objects of $\mathcal P_R$, replace its new upper-left vertex $Z$ by a K-flat flat-term resolution $T\to Z$ and precompose both arrows. The arrow required to be a denominator remains a quasi-isomorphism. For cancellation, if $sf=sg$ with $s$ a denominator and $f,g$ parallel arrows in $\mathcal P_R$, ambient right cancellation gives $t:Z\to\operatorname{dom}(f)$ a quasi-isomorphism with $ft=gt$; replace $Z$ by such a resolution and precompose $t$. All these equations are equations in the homotopy category, and all vertices now lie in its full subcategory $\mathcal P_R$. Thus $W_R$ admits right fractions. In Lean the membership predicate is defined literally on X.as. CochainComplex.exists_isKFlatResolutionIndependentCoefficients supplies the replacements at independent site object, site morphism and coefficient universes. Its exactness clause for monoidal tensorRight becomes the required IsFlatOnSite clause by transporting exactFunctor along siteSheafTensorRightIso from [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits].

proof.text: The inclusion induces $J:W_R^{-1}\mathcal P_R\to D(R)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], since $Q_R$ inverts $W_R$. For $P,Q\in\mathcal P_R$, represent an arbitrary $QP\to QQ$ by a roof $P\xleftarrow{s}Z\xrightarrow{f}Q$ using [lem-pc-right-fraction-representation]. A resolution $r:T\to Z$ from [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] replaces it by $P\xleftarrow{sr}T\xrightarrow{fr}Q$, a roof entirely in $\mathcal P_R$ with denominator in $W_R$. Hence $J$ is full. If two such roofs have the same image, [lem-pc-right-fraction-common-refinement] supplies a common vertex $Z$ and arrows $a_i:Z\to T_i$ with $s_1a_1=s_2a_2$ a quasi-isomorphism and $f_1a_1=f_2a_2$. Resolve $Z$ by $r:T\to Z$ and replace $a_i$ by $a_ir$. This is a common refinement within $\mathcal P_R$, so the roofs are equal there by the same cited criterion. Thus $J$ is faithful. Every object of $D(R)$ is represented by a complex and is isomorphic to its K-flat flat-term resolution, so $J$ is essentially surjective and is an equivalence. In particular $L=Q_R|_{\mathcal P_R}$ is itself a localization at $W_R$: composition with the equivalence $J$ preserves the universal property of the fraction localization.

proof.text: Total tensor defines a bifunctor on homotopy categories, not just complexes. Use the differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. If $f-f'=dh+hd$ in the first variable, $h\otimes1$ is a degree $-1$ homotopy on the total tensor: the two cross terms with the second differential cancel because $h$ lowers the first degree by one. If $g-g'=dk+kd$ in the second variable, the homotopy on the $(p,q)$ summand is $(-1)^p1\otimes k$; its two terms with the first differential cancel. The remaining terms give respectively $(f-f')\otimes1$ and $1\otimes(g-g')$. Consequently the complex bifunctor descends to $K(R)\times K(R)$ and then, after $Q_R$, gives $B(P,Q)=Q_R\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RQ)$ on $\mathcal P_R\times\mathcal P_R$. The proved source construction CategoryTheory.Functor.bifunctorMapHomotopyCategory implements these two tensor homotopies. Uncurrying it gives B; the requested complex-level comparison is the uncurried factorization isomorphism whiskeringLeft₂BifunctorMapHomotopyCategoryIso of that construction.

proof.text: The functor $B$ inverts $W_R$ in each variable. For a quasi-isomorphism $s:P\to P'$ and a K-flat $Q$, [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] says $C(s)$ is acyclic. By [def-pc-kflat-complex], $\operatorname{Tot}(C(s)\otimes_RQ)$ is acyclic. The cone formula of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and tensor differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] identify this total complex with $C(\operatorname{Tot}(s\otimes1_Q))$: distribute the finite sum $P'^a\oplus P^{a+1}$ over tensor and direct sums; on the shifted $P$ summands both differentials are $-d_P\otimes1+(-1)^{a}1\otimes d_Q$, and the off-diagonal term is $s\otimes1$. The cone criterion therefore makes $\operatorname{Tot}(s\otimes1_Q)$ a quasi-isomorphism. For the second variable use the chain symmetry $x_p\otimes y_q\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y_q\otimes x_p$, whose compatibility with the two differential terms follows by substituting $p+1$ and $q+1$ in the sign; the ordinary module symmetry is the balanced pure-tensor swap [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. It reduces the assertion to the first-variable argument with the K-flat first factor held fixed. Finally $Q_R$ sends these quasi-isomorphisms to isomorphisms. This uses no exactness of tensor on arbitrary complexes and no boundedness assumption. The Lean proof uses the independent-universe tensor additivity from [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits] (using symmetry for the other variable) and the two tensor-cone comparisons from the source module attached to [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso]. It constructs the bicomplex braiding componentwise, totalizes it, and composes with the signed mapBifunctorFlipIso. A pair of denominators is sent to the composite of the first-variable and second-variable quasi-isomorphisms.

proof.text: Use the product form of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], implemented by Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Localization.Prod through two successive localizations. Step 2 gives L = P.ι followed by Q_R as a localization at W_R. Hence L times L is a localization at W_R times W_R. Step 4 shows that H = (P.ι times P.ι) followed by B and Q_R inverts this product class. Localization.lift H along L times L constructs T, and the inverse of Localization.fac gives the requested natural representative comparison. For a denominator, invert its naturality square to obtain the equation for the inverse denominator. No representative choices or new unresolved statements are introduced.

proof.text: Apply the fully faithful precomposition clause of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to the product localization L times L from Step 5, with arbitrary target category E. Localization.fullyFaithfulWhiskeringLeft gives a fully faithful functor on functor categories. Its map_bijective theorem, specialized to U and V, is definitionally the displayed bijection on arbitrary natural transformations. Fullness gives existence of extensions and faithfulness gives uniqueness; invertibility of the transformation is not assumed.

The selected tensor is definitionally the original nested choice. Private cone proofs are generalized to avoid repeated site-specific construction; their mathematical argument is unchanged. The proved generic homotopy-bifunctor factorization and a generic map equation avoid unfolding the quotient construction in the site-specific proof.
